purpose: Eighth expanded public source layer focused on stapled peptides and peptidomimetic macrocycles, sulfated glycosaminoglycan and heparin mimetics, saponin glycosides, strained-ring bioactive motifs, sulfur-rich natural products, metal chelators and ionophores, macrocyclic kinase or bifunctional ligands, and photoredox/electrochemical route handles.

promotion_requirements: explicit precursor structures before template or proposal promotion
separate peptide, glycan, adjuvant, strained-ring, sulfur, metal-homeostasis, macrocycle, bifunctional-ligand, radical, photochemical, or electrochemical policy

route-specific stereochemistry, sequence, sulfation pattern, glycan topology, aglycone site, ring strain, sulfur oxidation state, metal selectivity, linker topology, redox handle, and activation-mode review

toxicology, immunology, anticoagulant, adjuvant, bioactive peptide, electrophile, antimicrobial, metal-homeostasis, kinase-inhibitor, photochemical, electrochemical, or radical-safety review where relevant
safety_scope: records intentionally avoid quantities, operational procedures, and synthesis conditions

bioactive peptide, anticoagulant-like, vaccine-adjuvant, strained electrophile, sulfur bioactivation, ionophore, kinase-inhibitor, photoredox, and electrochemical entries are high-level route priors only

families.name: Stapled peptides, peptidomimetics, and constrained peptide macrocycles
families.strategic_principle: Separate sequence, residue modification, macrocyclization or staple position, and delivery or target-engagement metadata from ordinary amide coupling. Macrocyclization is route-defining only when the biological topology and sequence context are explicit.

families.name: Glycosaminoglycan, heparin-like, and sulfated carbohydrate mimetics
families.strategic_principle: Expose chain length, sulfation pattern, uronic-acid or hexosamine identity, and protein-binding mode. Sulfated glycans and mimetics are not generic protected sugar routes.

families.name: Saponin, triterpenoid, steroidal glycoside, and adjuvant-like glycan arrays
families.strategic_principle: Separate aglycone preparation, glycan-array assembly, acyl chain or side-chain editing, and immunological or membrane-active context. Saponin glycosides require aglycone/site/glycan policy rather than blind glycosylation templates.

families.name: Bioactive strained rings: epoxides, aziridines, cyclopropanes, and azabicycles
families.strategic_principle: Treat ring strain, stereochemistry, ring-opening liability, and covalent or biosynthetic role as strategic metadata. Small strained rings are not interchangeable alkyl decorations.

families.name: Sulfur-rich natural products, isothiocyanates, thioethers, and sulfoxides
families.strategic_principle: Separate carbon skeleton assembly from sulfur incorporation, oxidation state, bioactivation, odor/reactivity liability, and biosynthetic origin. Sulfur state and release chemistry are route-defining.

families.name: Metal chelators, antidotes, ionophores, and metal-homeostasis modulators
families.strategic_principle: Separate ligand denticity, metal selectivity, ion transport, chelation or delivery role, and toxicology from ordinary heteroatom scaffold synthesis.

families.name: Macrocyclic kinase inhibitors, bivalent ligands, and topology-constrained binders
families.strategic_principle: Separate binding-vector selection, linker topology, macrocyclization timing, and target biology from generic macrocycle closure. A macrocycle or bivalent linker is strategic only with binding topology metadata.

families.name: Photoredox, electrochemical, and radical late-stage route handles
families.strategic_principle: Separate target structure from temporary redox handles, radical precursors, activation mode, site-selectivity evidence, and functional-group tolerance. Redox handles are route strategy metadata, not target fragments.

anchors.name: Sequence-defined peptide with reviewed staple, macrocycle, or peptidomimetic constraint
Sulfated glycan or mimetic with explicit chain length and sulfation pattern
Triterpenoid or steroidal aglycone with reviewed glycan array and acyl/side-chain policy
Strained epoxide, aziridine, cyclopropane, or azabicycle with stereochemical and reactivity policy
Sulfur-rich motif with oxidation-state, bioactivation, or biosynthetic-origin metadata
Chelator or ionophore with reviewed metal selectivity and homeostasis role
Macrocyclic or bivalent ligand with binding vectors, linker topology, and target context
Temporary redox, photochemical, or electrochemical handle with activation-mode and selectivity policy

disconnections.name: Stapled peptide to linear sequence plus macrocyclization or staple-position policy

break_bonds: modified residue pair to linear sequence boundary
forward_logic: identify the parent peptide sequence and residues that define the staple or macrocycle
separate linear sequence assembly from conformational constraint installation
track biological target, cell-penetration or stability rationale, and sequence fidelity
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward routes that preserve sequence identity and explain the staple or macrocycle topology rather than treating the closure as generic alkene or amide formation.

evidence.citation: Hydrocarbon-stapled peptide review covers principles, practice, and progress for stapled peptide design.
Peptide macrocyclization review discusses transition-metal-enabled peptide macrocyclization as a strategic constraint approach.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit sequence, staple position, and macrocycle topology

disconnections.name: Peptidomimetic residue set to parent sequence plus delivery or stability policy

break_bonds: peptidomimetic backbone or side-chain modification boundary
forward_logic: map modified residues to the parent sequence or pharmacophore
separate residue synthesis from sequence assembly and delivery/stability rationale
avoid scoring protected peptide intermediates as strategic completion without biological context
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use peptidomimetic entries only when residue identity and biological or delivery role are explicit.

evidence.citation: Hydrocarbon-stapled peptide review links conformational constraint to peptide therapeutic strategy.
Peptide macrocyclization review illustrates macrocycle formation as a route-defining peptide modification.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate only with parent-sequence mapping and delivery or stability rationale

disconnections.name: Sulfated glycosaminoglycan to chain-length, monosaccharide, and sulfation-pattern policy

target_features: uronic acid or amino sugar sequence

forward_logic: define chain length, residue order, and sulfation sites before route scoring
separate protected glycan assembly from late sulfation or mimetic installation
track protein-binding or anticoagulant-like context and avoid generic sugar-stock closure
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward routes that preserve sulfation topology and chain identity, not merely any sulfated carbohydrate.

evidence.citation: Heparin and heparin-mimetic review discusses heparin-like molecules and mimetics in biological context.
Sulfated alginate review discusses sulfated polysaccharides for biomedical applications.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit sulfation pattern, chain length, and binding-mode metadata

disconnections.name: Small-molecule or polymeric heparin mimetic to sulfate pharmacophore plus scaffold policy

target_features: non-glycan scaffold mimicking sulfated GAG charge pattern

forward_logic: separate scaffold synthesis from sulfate pharmacophore installation
track whether the motif mimics glycan topology, charge density, or protein-binding presentation
flag anticoagulant and promiscuous-binding context before proposal promotion
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Treat sulfate-rich mimetics as advisory unless the target protein-binding role and charge pattern are known.

evidence.citation: SPGG review discusses a sulfated small-molecule glycosaminoglycan mimetic and pharmacological effects.
Heparin-mimetic review frames heparin-like molecules and mimetics as biologically distinct from ordinary carbohydrates.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit charge-pattern and protein-binding rationale

disconnections.name: Saponin glycoside to aglycone plus glycan-array and acyl-side-chain policy

target_classes: cardiac glycosides outside bufadienolide seed scope
target_features: acyl chain or side-chain contribution to biological activity

forward_logic: define aglycone identity and glycosylation sites before route scoring
separate glycan-array assembly from aglycone synthesis or semisynthesis
track adjuvant, membrane-active, cardiotonic, or toxicity context
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward routes that expose aglycone/glycan/site boundaries and do not collapse complex saponins into generic glycosides.

evidence.citation: QS saponin biosynthesis review discusses heterologous biosynthesis and saponin structural complexity.
Quillaja saponin supply review discusses QS-21 scalability and supply context for adjuvanted vaccines.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit aglycone, glycan-array, acyl-chain, and biological-context metadata

disconnections.name: QS-like saponin to semisynthetic, biosynthetic, or supply-chain route policy

break_bonds: natural-source aglycone or glycoside pool boundary
forward_logic: separate total synthesis, semisynthesis, and biosynthetic-source strategies
track supply-chain, scalability, and immunology constraints without operational details
avoid treating natural saponin mixtures or advanced analogues as generic stock
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use QS-like saponin entries for source and route-policy critique, not automatic stock closure.

evidence.citation: QS saponin biosynthesis review provides public context for biosynthetic source strategies.
Quillaja saponin supply review highlights scalability and supply constraints for QS-21 demand.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit biosynthetic, semisynthetic, or supply-chain route rationale

disconnections.name: Epoxide or aziridine bioactive motif to strained-ring installation and ring-opening policy

break_bonds: strained C-O or C-N ring closure boundary
ring-opening electrophile to parent scaffold boundary
forward_logic: define whether the strained ring is a biosynthetic motif, warhead, or stereochemical handle
separate parent scaffold assembly from strained-ring installation
track stereochemistry, reactivity, and safety review before promotion
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Do not reward strained-ring routes unless ring strain, stereochemistry, and bioactive role are explicit.

evidence.citation: Cyclopropane natural-product biosynthesis review illustrates that strained rings can be biosynthetically and strategically distinct motifs.
Azabicyclohexane synthesis review provides public context for constrained nitrogen-containing strained-ring scaffolds.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit strained-ring role, stereochemistry, and reactivity policy

disconnections.name: Cyclopropane or azabicyclic motif to parent skeleton plus strain/topology policy

forward_logic: map the strained ring to the parent scaffold and conformational role
separate strained-ring construction from side-chain or substituent decoration
track stereochemistry, ring fusion, and natural-product or medicinal context
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Prefer routes that expose strain-building logic and topology instead of treating cyclopropanes as ordinary alkyl branches.

evidence.citation: Cyclopropane natural-product biosynthesis review supports treating cyclopropanes as source-backed strategic motifs.
Azabicyclohexane synthesis review covers a constrained bioactive ring family relevant to route critique.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit strained-ring topology and stereochemical mapping

disconnections.name: Sulfur-rich natural product to sulfur incorporation and oxidation-state policy

target_features: thioether, sulfoxide, sulfide, or polysulfide motif

break_bonds: C-S bond or sulfur insertion boundary
forward_logic: define sulfur oxidation state and connectivity before route scoring
separate carbon skeleton synthesis from sulfur incorporation or oxidation-state adjustment
track biosynthetic origin, reactivity, odor, and biological context
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward routes that preserve sulfur oxidation-state logic and do not flatten thioethers, sulfoxides, and isothiocyanates into generic heteroatom substituents.

evidence.citation: Marine sulfur natural-product review discusses chemistry and biology of sulfur-containing natural products.
Allium sulfur chemistry review discusses sulfur-compound chemistry relevant to natural-product route critique.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit sulfur state, incorporation timing, and biological context

disconnections.name: Glucosinolate or isothiocyanate motif to bioactivation and release-chemistry policy

target_features: food, botanical, or bioactive sulfur context

break_bonds: bioactivation precursor to active sulfur motif boundary
forward_logic: separate stable precursor, release handle, and active sulfur motif
track biological context and avoid treating bioactivated sulfur groups as inert substituents
flag electrophile and stewardship review before proposal promotion
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use glucosinolate/isothiocyanate entries for release-policy critique, not generic C-S disconnection.

evidence.citation: Sulfur-compound aroma review provides public context for volatile sulfur metabolites in vegetables and mushrooms.
Marine sulfur natural-product review supports sulfur bioactivity and reactivity as route-relevant metadata.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate only with explicit precursor, release, or bioactivation metadata

disconnections.name: Metal chelator to ligand arms, denticity, and metal-selectivity policy

break_bonds: chelating arm to central scaffold boundary
forward_logic: define donor atoms, denticity, and target metal before route scoring
separate ligand scaffold construction from metal-binding arm installation
track chelation, antidote, ferroptosis, cuproptosis, or homeostasis context
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward chelator routes only when denticity, metal selectivity, and biological role are explicit.

evidence.citation: Iron and copper chelator review discusses modulation of ferroptosis and cuproptosis by chelators and related agents.
Copper-homeostasis review discusses copper homeostasis and cuproptosis as therapeutic targets.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit donor set, metal selectivity, and homeostasis context

disconnections.name: Ionophore or metal-transport scaffold to binding cavity plus transport policy

break_bonds: ion-binding cavity to lipophilic scaffold boundary
forward_logic: separate ion-binding topology from hydrophobic transport scaffold
track target metal, transport role, and membrane or homeostasis context
avoid promoting ionophores as ordinary macrocycles or ligands without toxicology review
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Treat ionophore routes as advisory unless binding cavity, metal selectivity, and transport role are reviewed.

evidence.citation: Copper-homeostasis review frames metal transport and homeostasis as therapeutic intervention context.
Copper homeostasis and cuproptosis atherosclerosis review provides public context for metal-homeostasis intervention strategy.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit metal-binding topology and transport policy

disconnections.name: Macrocyclic kinase inhibitor to binding vectors plus macrocycle-closure policy

target_features: conformational constraint tied to potency or selectivity

break_bonds: macrocycle closure bond between binding vectors
forward_logic: identify kinase-binding core and the vectors used for macrocyclization
separate pharmacophore synthesis from macrocycle closure and conformational tuning
track target biology, selectivity, and resistance or allosteric rationale
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward macrocyclic kinase routes only when binding vectors and conformational rationale are explicit.

evidence.citation: Macrocyclic CDK inhibitor review discusses recent advances in macrocyclic kinase-inhibitor design.
Dual ALK inhibitor strategy review provides public context for scaffold and resistance strategy in kinase inhibitor design.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit binding vectors, macrocycle topology, and target-selectivity rationale

disconnections.name: Bivalent or bifunctional ligand to two binding modules plus linker-topology policy

target_features: defined linker length or exit vectors

break_bonds: second binding module to linker boundary
forward_logic: separate each binding module from the linker and topology constraint
track linker length, exit vectors, target proximity, and biological mechanism
avoid scoring bivalent molecules as generic linked fragments without target-context metadata
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use bivalent-ligand entries only when both binding modules and linker topology are explicitly mapped.

evidence.citation: Hsp70-Bim disruptor review includes small-molecule and peptidic disruptor context for topology-aware binding design.
Macrocyclic CDK inhibitor review supports topology-constrained ligand design as route-relevant medicinal chemistry context.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit module identity, linker topology, and biological mechanism

disconnections.name: Photoredox late-stage functionalization to parent scaffold plus temporary radical handle

target_classes: radical C-H or Minisci functionalization targets
target_features: temporary redox-active handle or radical precursor

break_bonds: late-stage C-C, C-N, C-S, or C-heteroatom bond traced to radical precursor
forward_logic: separate parent scaffold from the late-stage functionalization handle
track activation mode, site-selectivity evidence, and functional-group tolerance
remove temporary redox handles from target-stock reasoning
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward late-stage photoredox routes only when the temporary handle and site-selectivity rationale are explicit.

evidence.citation: Heterogeneous photocatalysis review discusses late-stage functionalization of complex molecules.
Late-stage functionalization update discusses LSF in current drug-discovery context.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit parent scaffold, temporary handle, activation mode, and site-selectivity evidence

disconnections.name: Electrochemical or redox-handle route to parent scaffold plus activation-mode policy

break_bonds: redox-active precursor to product bond boundary
forward_logic: identify which group is a temporary redox handle and which atoms remain in the target
separate electrochemical activation strategy from structural target features
track oxidation/reduction window, selectivity, and scale/safety review at a high level
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use electrochemical entries for route-boundary critique and prevent redox handles from being treated as target fragments.

evidence.citation: Late-stage functionalization overview discusses LSF strategies in drug discovery.
Late-stage functionalization update provides public context for modern LSF route strategy.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit redox handle, activation mode, and site-selectivity metadata

source_notes.summary: The v9 expansion promotes the next backlog families for stapled peptides, sulfated glycan mimetics, saponins, strained-ring bioactive motifs, sulfur-rich natural products, metal chelators and ionophores, macrocyclic/bifunctional ligands, and photoredox/electrochemical route handles.

Bioactive peptide, anticoagulant-like, vaccine-adjuvant, electrophilic strained-ring, organosulfur bioactivation, metal-homeostasis, kinase-inhibitor, bifunctional-ligand, radical, photochemical, and electrochemical records are advisory. Promotion to proposal generation requires explicit biological-mode, toxicology, immunology, stewardship, metal-homeostasis, photochemical, electrochemical, or radical-safety review as applicable.
